title: Harmony: Bix's whole tones and Condon's four-string guitar
summary: They discuss Bix's whole-tone surprise, Condon's big majors and why four-string guitar sounds sharper.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: I see in the elements of the Chicago style do you recall anything specifically regarding their attitude toward harmonics? they used the harmonics of the original tune they modified them anybody have ideas there?
I can remember the general excitement around when Bix pulled the first whole tone that surprised everybody and everybody worked on it vigorously from then on
instead of a chromatic why he used whole tone? yeah

the idea of of using good and better chords and clever ones or unusual ones was quite consciously done by everybody particularly piano players I think Condon was the first one who ever started using these great big majors and who began thinking in terms of Bach really
but he had only four strings didn't he?

yes but he still does it Condon can get more majors into one chorus than any human I've ever heard in my life Condon as a matter of fact is of all the really close friends I've got is the only one I'm afraid to play with not just because he can get critical very quickly but but because he's so absolutely accurate

you hear so little of Condon yet what I hear is good and such remarkable respect for his play with four strings he seems to be satisfied that he's doing all he wants to do he doesn't need the six and yet he certainly would be capable on six wouldn't he if he wanted to
